learning_outcomes.text: Know the general specific legislative framework applicable to the field of mechanical and mechatronic engineering;
Understand legislation regarding occupational safety, industrial security, and health standards applicable to engineering activities;
Possess detailed notions about regulations concerning road traffic, collective labor agreements, safety signage, manual handling of loads, and use of work equipment;
Know the implications of regulations concerning noise, electromagnetic fields, and working with display screens;
Understand the role and applicability of specific safety norms in particular engineering activities (internal transport, unconventional machining, etc.).
Identify and correctly interpret applicable legislation for various engineering situations encountered in practice;
Apply legal provisions in risk assessment, occupational safety, and workplace organization;
Elaborate and support simple technical-legal documents, such as reports, syntheses, or legislative-themed papers;
Actively participate in debates, applied discussions, and case analyses regarding engineering norms and regulations;
Efficiently utilize updated legislative sources (Official Monitor, legal platforms, specialized bibliography).
Assume responsibility for observing the professional code of ethics and specific legal provisions in the technical field;
Act responsibly in the context of regulations concerning health, occupational safety, and protection of technical personnel;
Actively contribute to maintaining a safe working environment in compliance with legal norms;
Demonstrate autonomy in legislative documentation and in applying rules to practical situations;
Demonstrate critical thinking, integrity, and fairness in interpreting and applying regulations in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction
Decision no. 600 of June 13, 2007, regarding the protection of young people at the workplace
Law no. 49 of March 8, 2006, for the approval of Government Emergency Ordinance no. 195/2002 regarding road traffic
Unique collective labor agreement at the national level for the years 2007-2010
Decision no. 971 of July 26, 2006, regarding minimum requirements for safety and/or health signage at the workplace
Decision no. 493 of April 12, 2006, regarding minimum safety and health requirements related to workers' exposure to risks generated by noise
Decision no. 1136 of August 30, 2006, regarding minimum safety and health requirements related to workers' exposure to risks generated by electromagnetic fields
Decision no. 1028 of August 9, 2006, regarding minimum safety and health requirements for the use of display screen equipment
Decision no. 1051 of August 9, 2006, regarding minimum safety and health requirements for manual handling of loads that present risks to workers, especially musculoskeletal disorders
Decision no. 1146 of August 30, 2006, regarding minimum safety and health requirements for the use of work equipment by workers
Decision no. 1091 of August 16, 2006, regarding minimum safety and health requirements for the workplace
Law no. 31 of March 22, 1991, regarding the establishment of working hours under 8 hours per day for employees working in special conditions - harmful, heavy, or dangerous
Occupational Safety Law no. 90 of July 12, 1996
Law no. 307 of July 12, 2006, regarding fire protection
NSSM 8 maintenance and repairs
Occupational safety norms for internal transport
N.S.S.M. no. 23/2000; Specific occupational safety norms for transport
Occupational safety norms for painting activities
Specific occupational safety norms for unconventional machining
N.S.S.M. 37/1996 - Specific occupational safety norms for automatic data processing; specific occupational safety norms for compressed air production activities
teaching_methods: Presentations on the board of the studied issues
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the Colloquium and Seminar components.
